why_ai: Food must be received, cut, stocked and sold in a physical store, and shoppers keep buying groceries in person even as ordering and pricing automate.
why_clarity: Sales, shrink and in-stock are measured daily across thousands of near-identical items and transactions.
why_digital: Physical food is handled in a local store and bought mostly in person, with online orders still picked and handed over physically.

why_ai: Forecasting automates, but the read of product condition and the cull still happen by hand on the floor.
why_clarity: Shrink and in-stock show within days on thousands of daily order and markdown decisions, though managers order by feel.
why_digital: Orders and markdowns are set on screens from observations of physical product on displays and in coolers.

why_ai: Shelf-life-aware store ordering is a well-defined forecasting problem AI vendors already sell.
why_clarity: Each order's shrink and in-stock outcome is measured within days, though override practice varies by manager.
why_digital: Sales, on-hand and promotion data in, orders out, sold as software with some floor input.

why_ai: Markdown depth and timing follow from days-to-expiry and sales rate, a pricing problem AI handles well.
why_clarity: Each marked-down lot sells or is culled within days, repeated every day across thousands of items.
why_digital: Prices are computed on screens, but the product is physical and labels are often still printed and applied by hand.

why_ai: Interval forecasting and schedule optimisation are mature automation, with labour law and union rules as constraints.
why_clarity: Understaffed and overstaffed intervals are measurable every week across every store and department.
why_digital: Sales, traffic and truck data in, schedules out, all on workforce software sold remotely.

why_ai: Cutting subprimals and fish is skilled knife work under food-safety rules that no software performs.
why_clarity: Yield and margin per pound are measurable, but cutting choices are made by feel and vary by cutter.
why_digital: Physical meat is cut and wrapped by hand in a store back room, with paper logs.

why_ai: Sensors and scans capture records, but accountable staff must check temperatures, act on failures and answer inspectors.
why_clarity: Checks and data elements are codified and repeated daily, but adequacy is tested only by inspections or outbreaks.
why_digital: Records are increasingly digital, but they start from physical receiving, cooking and cooling in the store.

why_ai: Owner-run community supermarkets keep a local, physical role, though buying and deal reconciliation automate.
why_clarity: Deal entitlements and invoices are checkable, but buying on the deal book relies on owner judgement.
why_digital: Buying runs on portals and PDFs, but the store sells physical goods face to face in its town.

why_ai: Community knowledge, imported assortments and in-person shopping protect these chains, though forecasting can help buyers.
why_clarity: Seasonal leftovers are measurable after each festival, but import buying rests on buyers' cultural knowledge.
why_digital: Physical imported goods are sold in stores to community shoppers, with buying on spreadsheets and messaging apps.

why_ai: Applying written eligibility rules to item attributes is classification AI does well.
why_clarity: Each item is eligible or not under stated rules, across hundreds of thousands of items, with register rejections as feedback.
why_digital: Item files, waiver texts and product lists in, POS flags out, all digital.

why_ai: Picking from shared store aisles stays physical after the robotic warehouses retreated, though planning automates.
why_clarity: Each order is filled or not, item by item, with fill rate and minutes per order known immediately.
why_digital: Orders arrive online, but the work is walking aisles and the customer receives physical groceries.

why_ai: Consented cross-retailer purchase panels are an asset AI cannot generate, though reporting automates.
why_clarity: Panel metrics follow fixed definitions released on a regular calendar, though projections are estimates.
why_digital: Receipts and scans in, subscription dashboards out, sold to remote clients.

why_ai: Site forecasts guiding decade-long leases need modellers' judgement and client trust, though geospatial modelling automates.
why_clarity: Each forecast is a number, but whether it was right shows only after the store has traded for a year or more.
why_digital: Geodata and analog-store data are modelled on screens, with site visits and relationship-led selling.

why_ai: Price collection and gap reports automate readily, and online prices can be scraped by anyone.
why_clarity: Prices are exact and checked weekly across thousands of items and stores.
why_digital: Prices are collected online or by field checkers and delivered as digital reports.

why_ai: Task times can be estimated from scan streams, eroding manual time studies.
why_clarity: Standards are explicit seconds per task, checked against actual hours each week.
why_digital: Time studies start in stores, but standards and forecasts are built and delivered as software.

why_ai: Wholesale purchasing power and retailer relationships give leverage AI tools cannot replicate.
why_clarity: Category, pricing and ad plans recur weekly and are judged by store sell-through.
why_digital: Category and pricing work is done on screens, but programmes are sold through wholesaler reps and store visits.

why_ai: Own-brand specifications, supplier audits and member relationships need accountable people, though benchmarking automates.
why_clarity: Item launches and bids recur, judged by sales and quality audits over months.
why_digital: Strategy and bids are on screens, while quality audits and sensory tests handle physical product.

why_ai: Segmentation and offer targeting are standard machine learning that platforms and AI-native rivals already automate.
why_clarity: Offer redemptions and campaign results are measured quickly across millions of shoppers.
why_digital: Transaction and loyalty data in, offers and dashboards out, sold as software.

why_ai: Sanctioning stores is a statutory government power exercised by accountable officials, with adversarial trafficking cases.
why_clarity: Transaction-pattern alerts recur at scale, but investigations take months to resolve.
why_digital: EBT transaction data is analysed on screens, with store visits and letters to retailers.

why_ai: Alarm triage automates, but diagnosis and repair of rack systems still need refrigeration engineers.
why_clarity: Alarms, temperatures and leak rates are objective and repeated across thousands of stores.
why_digital: Controller data is monitored remotely, with technicians dispatched to the store.

why_ai: Settlement and price-limit checks automate, but authorisation decisions sit with state officials.
why_clarity: Rules, price limits and settlements are exact and repeated for every transaction.
why_digital: Card transactions and product lists are entirely digital, procured by states.

why_ai: Bankers sell on relationships and negotiate bespoke deals and divestitures AI cannot front.
why_clarity: Each deal is one-off, and whether the price or package was best is rarely known.
why_digital: Valuations are built on screens, but deals are won and negotiated in person.

why_ai: Named experts' credibility carries the advice, though surveys and writing automate.
why_clarity: Strategy projects are bespoke and their payoff shows years later; monthly surveys repeat.
why_digital: Surveys and reports are produced and delivered digitally, sold through speaking and relationships.

why_ai: Member trust and the association brand help, but survey analysis and writing automate.
why_clarity: Annual reports recur on fixed themes, with little objective check on their findings.
why_digital: Member surveys in, published reports out, all digital.

why_ai: Matching surplus to buyers is marketplace software, though the food still has to be collected in person.
why_clarity: Each listed item sells or is wasted within a day, repeated across thousands of stores.
why_digital: Listings and payments run in apps, but shoppers or charities collect physical food at the store.
